eyebrow: Statistics & Probability for Data Science · Chapter 5
subtitle: Lesson 23 · Hypothesis Testing

steps.label: One-sample
steps.sub: One mean vs. a fixed value

code:
days = rng.normal(3.4, 1, 25).round(1)
t, p = stats.ttest_1samp(days, 3.0)
print(round(days.mean(), 2),
      round(t, 3), round(p, 4))
# 3.38 2.055 0.0509
caption: Illustrative data. Just above 0.05 is not 'no difference'.

code:
mob = rng.normal(48, 14, 60).round(2)
desk = rng.normal(55, 20, 45).round(2)
t, p = stats.ttest_ind(
    desk, mob, equal_var=False)
print(round(desk.mean()
            - mob.mean(), 2))  # 7.91
print(round(t, 3), round(p, 4))
# 2.3 0.0246
caption: equal_var=False runs Welch's t-test.

code:
bef = rng.normal(80, 25, 20).round(2)
aft = bef + rng.normal(6, 12, 20)
t, p = stats.ttest_rel(aft, bef)
print(round(p, 4))    # 0.0011
r = stats.ttest_ind(aft, bef,
                    equal_var=False)
print(round(r.pvalue, 4))   # 0.2509
caption: Wrongly treating pairs as independent hides the effect.
